meta.title: Our AI and automation toolkit
meta.description: Sample catalog. Texts and ratings are placeholders to be replaced with your own.

studs.label: Browser
studs.description: Drives or reads a web browser

platforms.label: VS Code
platforms.summary: Code editor that hosts Copilot and its agent mode.
platforms.why: Copilot does not run on its own. Everyone who uses it needs the editor.
platforms.what: Microsoft's code editor. Extensions such as GitHub Copilot run inside it.
how: Install VS Code from the company software portal or the official download page.
Open it and sign in to the extensions you need.

installation.why: A standard installer, usually already present on developer machines.

usage.why: Familiar to developers, new for everyone else.

facts.text: VS Code runs on 64-bit Windows client versions (not Windows Server), on macOS and on Linux (for example Ubuntu 20.04, Debian 10, RHEL 8, Fedora 36, with glibc 2.28 or newer).

platforms.label: Node.js
platforms.summary: JavaScript runtime for MCP servers started with npx.
platforms.why: Playwright MCP is started through Node.js, so the runtime has to be there first.
platforms.what: A JavaScript runtime that runs outside the browser. Playwright MCP needs version 18 or newer.
how: Check it in a terminal with node --version.

installation.why: An installer is enough, but versions must match what the tools expect.

usage.why: Runs in the background. Nobody has to use it directly.

openPoints.text: Operating system support of Node.js and Python on desktop systems was not checked.

platforms.label: Python
platforms.summary: Runtime for MCP servers built with the Python SDK.
platforms.what: A programming language runtime. MCP servers written with the official Python SDK run on it.

bricks.name: GitHub Copilot
bricks.summary: AI assistant in the editor that can use tools.
bricks.why: Lets people hand routine work to an AI assistant without leaving the editor, and gives teams one place to reach every connected tool.
bricks.what: GitHub's AI assistant inside VS Code. In agent mode it plans a task and calls tools that are connected through MCP.
how: Install the GitHub Copilot extension in VS Code.
Sign in with your company GitHub account.
Switch the chat to agent mode and add the MCP servers it should use.

installation.why: A standard extension and a company sign-in. Adding MCP servers is a separate manual step.

usage.why: Works through chat. The results still need a human review.

bricks.name: Playwright MCP
bricks.summary: Lets an AI assistant operate a browser.
bricks.why: Repeats browser tasks and checks without anyone writing test code, so non-developers can ask for them in plain language.
bricks.what: An MCP server from Microsoft that gives an AI assistant the browser actions of Playwright. It can drive Edge.
how: Add the server to the MCP settings of your client with npx and @playwright/mcp@latest.
Select Edge with the msedge browser option.

installation.why: The first time, every piece is connected by hand: Node.js, the MCP entry and the browser option.

usage.why: Describe the check in plain language, then review what it did.

facts.text: Playwright MCP needs Node.js 18 or newer and starts with npx @playwright/mcp@latest.
VS Code can add the server from the command line with code --add-mcp.

bricks.name: Custom MCP server
bricks.summary: Any MCP server your teams write themselves.
bricks.why: Connects your own internal systems to the AI assistant without waiting for a vendor.
bricks.what: An MCP server built by your team with the official TypeScript or Python SDK.
how: Build the server with the matching official SDK.
Register it in the MCP settings of your client.

installation.why: Someone has to write, test and host the server first.

usage.why: Once registered it behaves like any other MCP server.

facts.text: The Model Context Protocol project publishes official TypeScript and Python SDKs.

bricks.name: Microsoft Edge
bricks.summary: The company browser, usable as an automation target.
bricks.why: Automations run in a browser your teams already use, so there is nothing new to roll out.
bricks.what: Microsoft's Chromium-based browser. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, and Playwright can launch it with the msedge option.
how: Select it by setting the browser option to msedge in Playwright MCP.

usage.why: Nothing to learn. It is driven through Playwright MCP.

facts.text: Edge runs on Windows, on macOS (macOS 13 or later for Edge 151 and newer) and on 64-bit Linux (Ubuntu 18.04, Debian 10, openSUSE 15.5 or Fedora 39 and later).

recipes.title: Browser checks without test code
recipes.why: People can check internal web apps by describing the check in plain language, instead of waiting for someone to write test scripts.
recipes.what: Copilot receives the request and calls Playwright MCP. Playwright drives Edge through the steps and reports back.
how: Register the Playwright MCP server in the Copilot MCP settings.
Set the browser option to msedge.
Ask Copilot in agent mode to run your first check.
recipes.example: Ask Copilot to log in to the portal and confirm the monthly report page loads.

installation.why: The initial manual connection of all tools: Node.js, the MCP entry, the browser option and Copilot agent mode.

usage.why: Describe the check in plain language and review the result.
